notes: SINGULUS builds vacuum-coating (PVD sputtering, PECVD, evaporation), wet-chemical and thermal process equipment. Solar is now the core: turnkey and tool-level lines for high-efficiency cells, including heterojunction (HJT). It has a history in CIGS/CdTe thin-film tools (the old Triumph/CNBM partnership) and in optical-disc equipment (CD/DVD/Blu-ray). Other markets include semiconductor, medical/life science (including the MEDLINE contact-lens platform), packaging, glass & automotive, and battery & hydrogen.

The Nov 10 SpaceX contract is for a turnkey HJT solar-cell production line. The first line is worth more than €60 million, with delivery in the first half of 2027, to support satellite manufacturing in Bastrop, Texas. SINGULUS says this is part of a strategic partnership (started March 2026) under which it is planning to deliver multiple additional lines, and that production will scale to support more than 100 GW of production equipment. The company did not say whether 100 GW is annual or cumulative, or how many further lines are already firm orders. pv magazine noted the same ambiguity. Treat only the first >€60M line as a signed, quantified order.

That SpaceX order was signed after Sep 30, so it is not in the €47.1M backlog. Adding it would more than double the booked backlog, and it is large relative to 9M sales of €60.4M and the ~€83M 2026 sales guide.

Triumph Science and Technology (a CNBM / China National Building Material unit), once the largest shareholder at 16.75% and a key thin-film customer and lender, sold that stake on Oct 21, 2026, to A1681X GmbH & Co. KG, whose principal shareholder is Roland Lacher, a SINGULUS co-founder and former CEO/supervisory-board chair. SINGULUS took a ~€22.75M SpaceX subordinated loan to repay Triumph loans and project advances; remaining Triumph supply contracts were terminated and €15.3M of orders were reversed. The companies say they will still work together on selected projects, service and joint initiatives.

CFO and long-time Executive Board member Markus Ehret will leave on Dec 31, 2026, by mutual agreement after 16 years, following the refinancing and Triumph unwind. Headcount was 325 on Sep 30 (290 at year-end 2025), mainly because of the Q2 acquisition of MASS GmbH’s business in Anröchte. The Q3 presentation lists headcount as 312; the Q3 report and Nov 11 press release say 325.

FY2025 was weak: sales €48.3M (from €75.9M) and EBIT −€11.7M (from −€0.7M). The 2026 guide of ~€83M sales and a small positive EBIT was confirmed with the 9M results. A significant share is expected from Solar.

bull.text: A signed >€60M SpaceX HJT line, with a stated plan for more lines and a partnership in place since March 2026, is large relative to today’s sales and came with long-term SpaceX financing
9M sales were up about 36% to €60.4M and EBIT turned positive at €1.2M; the company confirmed its ~€83M sales / small positive EBIT guide for 2026

The March and October 2026 SpaceX loans refinanced the 2016 corporate bond and repaid Triumph, stretching core debt financing out about five years and, in the auditors’ view of the 2025 accounts, removing previously existing substantial going-concern doubt

bear.text: Equity is still negative (€64.8M) and liquidity risk “remains significant”: 2026–27 cash depends on customer payments arriving on time and on winning new projects. A single delayed or cancelled project is hard to offset

Only the first SpaceX line (>€60M) is a quantified signed order. Additional lines and “more than 100 GW of production equipment” are plans, not booked backlog. The business is now highly dependent on SpaceX

The stock more than doubled on Nov 11 (Xetra close €26.50, +108.7% from €12.70) and was last at €22.00 in the Nov 12 session after a €28.10 high. At ~€196M of market cap, the shares already price in a lot of future lines. The U.S. OTC line is not a usable market

Long history of restructuring, a 2016 capital reduction, a 4.5% corporate bond (redeemed early in 2026 at 105%), and Chinese-shareholder/lender support. FY2025 missed badly (sales €48.3M, EBIT −€11.7M). The finance chief is leaving at year-end

runContext.title: What kind of company this is, and is it on a Futura list?
runContext.summary: SINGULUS is a small German Prime Standard machinery company. It is not on Growth, Risk It, Early Inflection, Experiment, Piotroski, Magic Formula or Insider Buys. Those screens are built for liquid U.S.-listed stocks with StockAnalysis and Nasdaq data. This name is listed in Frankfurt (SNG) and only quoted as Pink Limited OTC in the U.S. (SGTSF), with a market cap near €200M, so it fails the usual size, listing and data-coverage tests even before the rules are scored.

runContext.signalsTitle: Why it isn’t on a list
signals: The screens need a U.S. listing, liquid Nasdaq/NYSE (or comparable) prices, and StockAnalysis financials. SGTSF fails that data test, and SNG is a euro-priced Xetra stock.
Even if the rules were applied by hand, the ~€196M cap is far below Growth’s $10B minimum, and Pink Limited OTC trading is not usable liquidity.
This card is a research file for a supplier in the SpaceX/Tesla orbit, not a claim that the stock passes a Futura screen.
runContext.caveat: Nothing here changes screener rules. Grades are partial: only Momentum can be scored, and it uses Xetra prices, not Nasdaq.

In the Nov 12 session the stock opened at €27.00, traded as high as €28.10 and as low as €21.50, and was last at €22.00 after the 17:30 CET close, down about 17% from the prior close, with volume around 448,000. news.title: 9M sales up about 36% to €60.4M; EBIT turns positive at €1.2M; 2026 guide confirmed
news.summary: Gross margin rose to 35.4% from 32.5%. Q3 sales were €15.1M with EBIT of −€1.4M. Underlying 9M order intake doubled to €60.3M before a €15.3M Triumph write-off; backlog was €47.1M at Sep 30. The company still expects about €83.0M of 2026 revenue and positive EBIT in the low single-digit millions. Markus Ehret will leave the Executive Board on Dec 31.

news.title: Signs a SpaceX contract for a turnkey HJT solar-cell line worth more than €60M
news.summary: Delivery is planned in the first half of 2027 as SpaceX expands satellite manufacturing in Bastrop, Texas. SINGULUS called it part of a strategic partnership begun in March 2026, under which it plans to deliver multiple additional lines, and said production will scale to support more than 100 GW of production equipment. SpaceX also provided funding in March and, as a subordinated secured loan, in October. The first trading session after the after-hours release was Nov 11, when Xetra more than doubled.

news.title: Inside-information disclosure of the SpaceX supply contract, published at 19:25 CET
news.summary: The same text as the company release, filed under Article 17 of the Market Abuse Regulation after the Xetra close (that day’s close was €12.70).

news.title: Takes a ~€22.75M subordinated loan and completes the sale of Triumph’s 16.75% stake
news.summary: The lender is the same technology partner that financed the company in March 2026 (later identified as SpaceX). Proceeds repaid all remaining Triumph loans and project advances, ending the related delivery obligations. Triumph sold its block to A1681X GmbH & Co. KG (Roland Lacher). Denan Chu left the Supervisory Board.

news.title: Agrees a long-term Solar partnership and five-year refinancing with a “leading global technology company”
news.summary: The March release did not name the partner. Later filings and the SpaceX contract announcement identified it as SpaceX and put the new financing at €29M, used to refinance the corporate bond, super-senior loans and a Chinese-bank loan. The 2016 4.5% bond (face €12.0M, redeemed at 105%) was repaid early on March 24, 2026.

gradeNote: StockAnalysis and Nasdaq, the usual grade sources, do not carry usable data for SGTSF or SNG, so three of the four letter grades are n/a (the same kind of gap you see when inputs are missing on a name like NMCO). Momentum is scored from delayed Xetra closes (Yahoo Finance, SNG.DE) against the current Growth / Risk It / Early Inflection reference pool, plus this ticker: +192% over 3 months, +362% over 6 months and +1,500% over 1 year through the Nov 12 last, vs SPY’s +11.16% 1-year change from the Nov 1 grade run. That ranks as A+. It is almost entirely the 2026 rerating, including the Nov 11 gap after the SpaceX contract, and it can reverse quickly — as the Nov 12 session already showed. Do not read A+ momentum as a quality or value grade.
